title: Cardamonin ameliorates neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease by regulating NF-kappaB signaling.
authors: Xia, Yezi; Zhang, Yinwei; Li, Ying; Li, Xiaojing; Wu, Yaling; Yao, Qi
one_liner_zh: 该文通过机器学习筛选帕金森病炎症相关基因并用分子对接验证豆蔻明与RELA结合，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作（NF-κB）但核心是药物抗炎机制，非TF-DNA结合建模研究。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation can accelerate neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease (PD). This study aims to identify biomarkers related to PD inflammation and investigate the function of cardamonin (CD) on microglia and neurons. METHODS: The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in PD were screened out. Inflammation-related genes (IRGs) were obtained from the GSEA and GeneCards databases. The protein-protein interaction network was constructed, and three machine learning algorithms, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis, random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM) were used to screen the core IRGs in PD pathogenesis. Potential drugs for core genes were screened through the ITCM and HERB databases, and the binding activity between the core targets and the drugs was verified by molecular docking. BV2 cells were induced with MPP + to construct a PD model. CCK-8 assay, flow cytometry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays, qPCR and western blotting were conducted to explore the function of CD on the activation of microglia and injury of neurons.. RESULTS: One thousand one hundred eighty-three DEGs and 518 IRGs were obtained, and 31 genes were in the intersection, among which v-rel reticuloendotheliosis viral oncogene homolog A (RELA, p65), a crucial component in NF-kappaB signaling, was upregulated in the PD samples and demonstrated good diagnostic efficacy. CD had good binding ability with RELA. CD significantly improved the viability, repressed apoptosis, reduced the production of pro-inflammatory factors (TNF-alpha, IL-6 and IL-1beta) of BV2 cells, which were induced by MPP+. In addition, CD significantly inhibited the activation of the NF-kappaB signaling pathway and the nuclear translocation of RELA. CONCLUSION: CD inhibits the inflammatory response of PD induced by microglia by targeting RELA and regulating the activation of NF-kappaB signaling.
abstract_zh: 背景：神经炎症可加速帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）中的神经退行性变。本研究旨在识别与PD炎症相关的生物标志物，并探讨豆蔻明（cardamonin, CD）对小胶质细胞和神经元的功能。方法：筛选出PD中的差异表达基因（differentially expressed genes, DEGs）。从GSEA和GeneCards数据库获取炎症相关基因（inflammation-related genes, IRGs）。构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络，并采用三种机器学习算法，即最小绝对收缩和选择算子（least absolute shrinkage and selection operator, LASSO）回归分析、随机森林（random forest, RF）和支持向量机（support vector machine, SVM），筛选PD发病机制中的核心IRGs。通过ITCM和HERB数据库筛选核心基因的潜在药物，并通过分子对接验证核心靶点与药物之间的结合活性。用MPP+诱导BV2细胞构建PD模型。采用CCK-8实验、流式细胞术、酶联免疫吸附实验、qPCR和western blotting探讨CD对小胶质细胞活化和神经元损伤的功能。结果：获得1183个DEGs和518个IRGs，其中31个基因位于交集内，其中v-rel网状内皮增生病毒癌基因同源物A（RELA, p65），作为NF-kappaB信号传导中的关键组分，在PD样本中上调并显示出良好的诊断效能。CD与RELA具有良好的结合能力。CD显著改善了MPP+诱导的BV2细胞的活力，抑制了凋亡，减少了促炎因子（TNF-alpha、IL-6和IL-1beta）的产生。此外，CD显著抑制了NF-kappaB信号通路的激活和RELA的核转位。结论：CD通过靶向RELA并调节NF-kappaB信号的激活，抑制由小胶质细胞诱导的PD炎症反应。
